title: Pressure Switch Did Not Close
shortDescription: The draft pressure switch did not close within the allowed window after the inducer started.
fullDescription: This York fault means the inducer motor energized but the pressure switch never sensed enough negative pressure to close its contacts. The control aborts the trial-for-ignition because operating without confirmed venting can release combustion gases into the home.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Blocked exhaust or intake terminal (snow, ice, debris, nest)
Plugged condensate trap on a high-efficiency model

symptoms: Inducer runs continuously without burner ignition
Furnace cycles inducer on and off chasing the switch
No heat output even though the thermostat is calling
Water dripping or pooling near a high-efficiency unit

fixSteps.title: Inspect Vent Terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Walk outside and verify the exhaust and intake pipes are clear of snow, leaves, and animal nests. Clear any obstruction with a non-metallic tool.

fixSteps.title: Check the Pressure Switch Hose
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the small rubber hose from the pressure switch, blow through it to clear water, and confirm it is firmly seated at both ends.

fixSteps.title: Service the Condensate Trap
fixSteps.instruction: On 90%+ efficiency furnaces, pour a cup of warm water through the inducer drain port to flush the trap. Reinstall and confirm free drainage.

fixSteps.title: Measure Switch Operation
fixSteps.instruction: With the inducer running, measure differential pressure at the switch port; compare to the spec on the switch (often -0.40 to -1.20 inches WC). Below spec means inducer or venting issue, not a bad switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace Inducer or Switch as Needed
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the pressure switch only if the differential pressure is correct but contacts will not close. Otherwise replace the inducer assembly with the OEM part.

whenToCallPro: If venting and condensate are clear but the switch still will not close, an inducer or board issue is likely and should be diagnosed by a licensed technician.

faq.q: Why does this happen more often in winter?
faq.a: Snow drifts and ice can block sidewall vent terminations, especially during heavy storms.

faq.q: Can I bypass the pressure switch with a jumper?
faq.a: Never. The switch is the primary safety preventing operation with blocked venting and CO buildup.

faq.q: My condensate line freezes outdoors — what now?
faq.a: Re-route the condensate to an interior drain. Frozen condensate is a common cause of repeated pressure-switch faults.

title: Open Limit Switch — Overheat Detected
shortDescription: The high-limit switch opened because supply-air temperature exceeded the safe threshold.
fullDescription: This York fault posts when the high-limit switch detects supply-air temperature above the design ceiling, usually because airflow across the heat exchanger is too low. The control turns the gas off, runs the blower to purge heat, and reports the limit-trip code until temperatures normalize.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Severely clogged air filter restricting return airflow
Closed or blocked supply registers / collapsed flex duct
Failed or weak blower motor / capacitor

symptoms: Furnace fires briefly then shuts down
Blower runs long after the burners cut off
Hot air from supply registers followed by cold air
Burner cycle time noticeably shorter than normal

fixSteps.title: Replace the Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and replace the return-air filter with the correct size and MERV rating. A 1" filter clogged with dust is the single most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Open All Supply Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the home and confirm every supply register is open and unblocked by furniture, rugs, or curtains. Closing too many registers raises static pressure dramatically.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the Blower Wheel
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, remove the blower assembly and check the wheel for caked dust. A coated wheel can lose 30%+ of its airflow.

fixSteps.title: Test Blower Motor and Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure capacitor microfarads and confirm they are within 6% of rated. Verify the motor reaches commanded RPM at heat speed.

fixSteps.title: Verify the Limit Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity across the limit switch at room temperature; it should be closed. If open cold, replace with the exact OEM part — limit switches are calibrated to the cabinet.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is verified normal but the limit still trips, the heat exchanger may be cracked or the gas input is overfired — both require a licensed technician.

faq.q: Can I jumper the limit switch to keep heat?
faq.a: No. Bypassing the limit can cause heat-exchanger damage and carbon-monoxide release.

faq.q: How often should I change my filter?
faq.a: Every 1–3 months for 1" pleated filters; 4–6 months for thicker media filters.

faq.q: Why does the blower keep running after lockout?
faq.a: It is intentionally purging residual heat from the heat exchanger to protect components.

title: Auxiliary Limit Open — Blower Compartment Overheat
shortDescription: The auxiliary high-limit in the blower compartment opened due to high temperature.
fullDescription: This York fault indicates the auxiliary or rollout-style limit located in the blower compartment opened because temperature exceeded its setpoint. It usually points to airflow restriction or a delayed blower start.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Restricted return air or extremely dirty filter
Blower fails to start on heat call
Overfired furnace — gas pressure too high

symptoms: Lockout posted shortly after burner light-off
Blower start is delayed or absent
Audible hum from blower without rotation
Hot air pocket inside cabinet when accessed

fixSteps.title: Replace the Filter and Open Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Install a clean filter and confirm all supply registers are open. Restricted return is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Blower Starts on Heat Call
fixSteps.instruction: Watch the blower for a clean start within the configured fan-on delay. Stalled or slow start indicates motor or capacitor issues.

fixSteps.title: Test Blower Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure microfarads with the unit off. Replace any capacitor reading more than 6% off rated value.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Auxiliary Limit
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity across the auxiliary limit cold. Replace with exact OEM part if open.

fixSteps.title: Verify Manifold Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm gas manifold pressure matches the rating-plate value. Overfiring can repeatedly trip auxiliary limits.

whenToCallPro: If the blower will not start, manifold pressure is wrong, or the limit reopens after a verified-clean airflow path.

faq.q: Is the auxiliary limit the same as the main limit?
faq.a: No. It is a secondary device, often a one-time fuse, located closer to the blower compartment.

faq.q: Can I run the system on emergency heat?
faq.a: Most furnaces do not have a non-gas backup. Use space heaters safely until the system is repaired.

faq.q: How fast can the limit re-trip?
faq.a: If the cause is uncorrected, often within 1–3 cycles.

title: Ignition Failure — Hot Surface Igniter Fault
shortDescription: The hot surface igniter is not heating to the temperature needed to light the burners.
fullDescription: This York furnace fault indicates the hot surface igniter (HSI) failed to reach proper glow temperature, or the control board sensed an open circuit on the igniter output. Without a glowing igniter the gas valve will not be authorized to open, so the burners never light and the cycle aborts after the trial-for-ignition period.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Cracked or burned-out hot surface igniter
Loose or corroded igniter wiring connection
Weak igniter — resistance drifting outside spec
Improper line voltage to the furnace

symptoms: Burners never light during a call for heat
Inducer runs but no glow visible at the igniter
Repeated retries followed by hard lockout
Cold air from registers when the blower runs

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle the Furnace
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the furnace disconnect off for 60 seconds, then back on, and watch the next ignition attempt through the inspection port.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the Igniter Visually
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the burner cover and look for a cracked, broken, or whitened igniter element. Any visible damage means replace it.

fixSteps.title: Measure Igniter Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, disconnect the igniter and measure resistance across its leads. A healthy silicon-nitride HSI typically reads 40–90 ohms; older silicon-carbide types read 50–200 ohms. Open or out-of-range = replace.

fixSteps.title: Check Igniter Connector and Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the molex/spade connector for corrosion, melted plastic, or loose pins. Reseat firmly and look for chafed wires along the routing.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Install the manufacturer-specified igniter, handling only by the ceramic base — skin oils shorten igniter life. Confirm the tip aligns with the carryover slot per the service manual.

whenToCallPro: If the new igniter also fails, if line voltage is unstable, or if the control board's igniter output reads incorrect voltage during trial-for-ignition.

faq.q: How long does a furnace igniter last?
faq.a: Most hot surface igniters last 4–7 years. Frequent short-cycling and handling the element with bare fingers shorten that life significantly.

faq.q: Can I clean an igniter instead of replacing it?
faq.a: No. The ceramic element cannot be cleaned safely. If it is contaminated or cracked, replacement is the only fix.

faq.q: Why did my new igniter fail quickly?
faq.a: The most common cause is touching the element with bare fingers during installation. Skin oils create hot spots that crack the ceramic.

title: Flame Rollout Switch Tripped
shortDescription: A flame rollout switch detected flame outside the burner enclosure and shut the furnace down.
fullDescription: This York fault is one of the most serious furnace faults. A rollout switch — a one-time or manual-reset thermal device near the burner box — opened because flame escaped the heat exchanger. Causes include blocked heat exchanger, weak inducer, or cracked exchanger. Operation must not resume until the cause is identified by a technician.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Severely sooted or blocked heat exchanger passages
Failed or weak inducer motor (insufficient draft)

symptoms: Furnace will not restart even after power cycling
Soot or scorch marks on the burner cover
Yellow rather than blue flame at the burners

fixSteps.title: Stop Using the Furnace
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the system off at the thermostat and the disconnect. Close the gas supply at the unit shutoff. Do not attempt to reset the rollout switch.

fixSteps.title: Verify CO Detector Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Test all CO detectors on the level with the furnace. If any alarm or read above 9 ppm, ventilate the home and call for service immediately.

fixSteps.title: Document the Symptom
fixSteps.instruction: Note any soot, melted wiring, or warped sheet metal near the burners. Photos help the technician diagnose faster.

fixSteps.title: Schedule Professional Service
fixSteps.instruction: A flame rollout requires a combustion analysis, draft test, and heat-exchanger inspection — all licensed-tech work.

fixSteps.title: Do Not Bypass the Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Resetting or jumping the rollout switch without correcting the cause can lead to a fire and CO release. Wait for service.

repairTime: Professional service same-day to several days
whenToCallPro: Always. Flame rollout is never a DIY repair — there is no safe way to operate the furnace until a technician has inspected the heat exchanger and venting.

faq.a: Flame outside the burner box can ignite nearby materials and indicates that combustion gases — including CO — may be entering the home.

faq.q: Will the rollout switch reset itself?
faq.a: Most modern rollout switches are manual-reset only. The technician will reset after correcting the underlying issue.

faq.q: Could a dirty filter cause this?
faq.a: Indirectly. Restricted airflow over time can warp the heat exchanger, leading to cracks that allow rollout.

title: Gas Valve Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The control board cannot drive the gas valve, or its feedback is out of range.
fullDescription: On this York furnace the integrated control sends 24 VAC to the main gas valve during trial-for-ignition, but the valve either does not open, draws unexpected current, or fails open-coil checks. The system locks out before any gas is released to the burners.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Open or shorted gas valve solenoid coil
Loose, broken, or corroded gas valve wiring

symptoms: No gas flow even with a glowing igniter
Audible relay click but no valve opening sound
Lockout posted on the first ignition attempt
Repeated retries with no flame ever established

fixSteps.title: Verify 24 VAC at Valve
fixSteps.instruction: With a multimeter on the gas valve terminals during trial-for-ignition, confirm 24 VAC ±10%. No voltage means a board or wiring issue, not a valve issue.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Valve Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check both leads for cracked insulation, loose spades, or green corrosion. Reseat or replace the harness as needed.

fixSteps.title: Test Valve Coil Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, measure across the coil terminals. Most 24 VAC valves read 30–80 ohms. Open or near-zero means the valve is bad.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Transformer Output
fixSteps.instruction: At the control transformer, verify 24–28 VAC under load. A weak transformer can drop voltage enough to keep the valve from pulling in.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Gas Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Replacement of the gas valve is a licensed-trade operation requiring a leak test on every joint with electronic detector and soap solution. Do not attempt without proper certification.

whenToCallPro: Replacement of any gas valve, regulator, or piping must be done by a licensed gas technician — a leak after reassembly is life-threatening.

faq.q: Can I clean a sticking gas valve?
faq.a: No. Modern valves are sealed and not field-serviceable. Replace, do not disassemble.

faq.q: How much does a furnace gas valve cost?
faq.a: Parts run $60–$220 depending on model. Professional replacement with leak test is typically $300–$700.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using the furnace?
faq.a: If the lockout repeats, leave the system off and the gas closed. Intermittent valve faults can become hazardous quickly.

title: Flame Sensed Out of Sequence
shortDescription: The control board detects flame at a time when the gas valve should be closed.
fullDescription: This York fault means the flame-sense rod is reporting flame current when no flame should be present — typically before the gas valve opens or after the trial-for-ignition has ended. The control treats this as a serious safety condition and locks the furnace out to prevent unburned gas accumulation.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Flame sensor shorted to ground or chassis
Moisture or carbon bridging on the flame-sense rod
Faulty integrated control module misreading sensor

symptoms: Furnace locks out immediately on call for heat
Burners may briefly fire then shut off with lockout
Diagnostic LED reports flame-sense fault repeatedly
No heat output despite thermostat calling

fixSteps.title: Cut Power and Inspect Burners
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off power and gas. Remove the burner cover and look for soot, water staining, or a flame sensor touching metal.

fixSteps.title: Clean the Flame-Sense Rod
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rod and gently polish with fine emery cloth. Wipe with a clean rag — do not use sandpaper coarser than 400 grit.

fixSteps.title: Verify Sensor Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the rod is not contacting the burner shell or any metal support. Reposition so it sits in the flame envelope without grounding.

fixSteps.title: Check for Gas Valve Leakby
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition disabled, watch the burners for any flame after the inducer purge. A momentary flame indicates a leaking gas valve, which must be replaced by a licensed pro.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Wiring to Board
fixSteps.instruction: Measure continuity from the sensor terminal back to the control board. Replace any harness that shows shorts to ground or open conductors.

whenToCallPro: Any time a leaking gas valve is suspected, the smell of gas is present, or the lockout returns immediately after cleaning the sensor.

faq.q: Is flame sensed when off a serious fault?
faq.a: Yes. It can mean unburned gas is entering the heat exchanger, which is a fire and CO hazard. Do not bypass the lockout.

faq.q: Can I keep using the furnace until a tech arrives?
faq.a: No. Leave the furnace off and the gas supply closed until the cause is identified.
Most modern furnaces show 1.5–6 microamps of DC flame current with a clean rod and stable flame.
